purpose: This plane shows complex numbers as points. You multiply, take conjugates and divide, and see each operation as a move on the plane. You find out that multiplying turns and stretches, and a number times its conjugate is always real.

stops.title: The complex plane
stops.text: Across is the real part and up is the imaginary part. Each number is an arrow with a dot at the tip. In steps 2 and 3, drag the dot with the brass ring (z). It snaps to whole numbers from -3 to 3. Red shows the result.
stops.try: In step 2, drag z and watch the red result point move with it.

stops.title: FOIL examples
stops.text: In step 1, choose one of three products. Then answer each multiple-choice step: First, Outer, Inner, Last, then the real and imaginary parts. A wrong answer says why, and you try again.
stops.try: Do Example 1, then press Example 2 for a new one.

stops.title: Multiply z by
stops.text: In step 2, pick a multiplier w (i, 2, 1+i and more). The readout lists the modulus (distance from 0) and angle of z, w and zw. You will see the distances multiply and the angles add.
stops.try: Choose i and see zw turn a quarter turn from z.

stops.title: Divide and solve
stops.text: In step 4, choose one of three tasks: a division and two equations. Each is a multiple-choice walk. For division you multiply the top and bottom by the conjugate of the bottom.
stops.try: Pick the division, then do the same with Solve z + 3.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 is FOIL multiplying. Step 2 shows multiplying as a move. Step 3 is conjugates, where you try at least five different z. Step 4 is dividing and solving.

stops.title: Try practice problems
stops.text: Seven short problems. Pick an answer and read why. Use Hint if you are stuck. Press Back to the lesson to return. Nothing is saved.
stops.try: Press Start practice, then try Hint on the first problem.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: A few questions to finish. A wrong answer explains itself.

teacher: Project step 2 and have students test at least three pairs before saying the rule: moduli multiply and angles add. Misconception: students think the conjugate product z times z-bar can be negative or imaginary. Step 3 lets them try five z values to see it never is.
